title: UniversalH0ProjectiveNormalization
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, choose D(R), and let P be a bounded cochain complex of finite projective R-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Suppose for every commutative R-algebra B that the termwise scalar extension B tensor P has zero homology in every negative degree and H0 is isomorphic as a B-module to B. Then there exists a bounded complex Q, each term explicitly a retract of a finite free R-module, with Q^n=0 for n<0 and d:Q^0→Q^1 zero, and Q(P) is isomorphic to Q(Q) in D(R). No scheme morphism or coefficient sheaf occurs.

proof.text: Induct on the number of negative degrees in a finite support interval. At the bottom negative term residue homology vanishing makes the differential residue-injective. The finite-projective residue criterion gives a finite projective cokernel locally at each prime, hence globally since it is finitely presented. Split and cancel the contractible pair. Each cancellation is a homotopy equivalence preserved by every scalar extension; repeat to obtain a connective bounded projective complex.

At each prime choose a minimal finite free model on an affine neighbourhood (0BCD). Negative terms have rank zero, and its zeroth term has rank one. For A=R_f the universal H0 hypothesis identifies ker(d0:A→A^m) with A. The kernel inclusion is multiplication by a non-zero-divisor a. Since a times each coordinate of d0(1) is zero, d0=0, including over nonreduced rings. Bounded projective representatives of the same derived object are homotopy equivalent, and these equivalences survive residue scalar extension. Consequently H0 of the connective projective model commutes with residue base change. The identity base change gives H0≅R.

Choose a generator of H0=R. Its cycle defines a residue-split injection R→Q0 at every prime, so its cokernel is finite projective by the residue criterion. Split off R globally. The remaining degree-zero summand maps residue-injectively into degree one, again giving a finite projective cokernel. Split and cancel that contractible pair. The result is connective, d0=0, and homotopy equivalent to the original P. Finite projective modules are retracts of finite free modules. The zero ring is handled by the zero complex.

lean.statement:
theorem universalH0_projective_normalization
    (R : Type v) [CommRing R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n))
    (hf : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite R (P.X n))
    (hp : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective R (P.X n))
    (hbase : ∀ (B : Type v) [CommRing B] (φ : R →+* B),
      let PB := ((ModuleCat.extendScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P
      (∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → IsZero (PB.homology i)) ∧
        Nonempty (PB.homology 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of B B)) :
    ∃ Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ,
      (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (Q.X n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ m : ℕ,
        ∃ (ι : Q.X n ⟶ ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} (Fin m) →₀ R))
          (π : ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{v} (Fin m) →₀ R) ⟶ Q.X n),
          ι ≫ π = 𝟙 (Q.X n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero (Q.X n)) ∧ Q.d 0 1 = 0 ∧
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)
